column1: # docxdriver 0.5.2 bugs found recording the write baseline (2026-11-13, oracle 1ffb0d7). Reproduce a case with
# `go run ./tools/oracle write show -plan <case> -ops <op>` (outputs under results/oracle/write-show/). The Go side
# fixes them; the entries below make compare count those cases as intended, never as expected Go behaviour.
# "track vs direct": the oracle breaks its own change-mode law for an Exact op (direct, accepted == track, accepted).
# W1 comment_set_status on a document without commentsIds/commentsExtensible parts adds their relationships and
#    content-type overrides but not the parts; its own gate refuses: "[Content_Types].xml: integrity: content type
#    Override names a missing part; ... relationship commentsIds targets a missing part". The op cannot succeed there.
# W2 comment_reply on tdf153804, tdf153526_commentInNumbering and the dirty fixtures: the reply has no range or
#    reference and its paraIdParent names nothing; gate: "w:comment has no commentReference; commentEx paraIdParent
# W3 direct replace_text / revise_text (and text.insert's equivalent) drop the replaced text's run properties; track
# keeps them. write:mixed bold "gamma" -> "gamma INSERTED": track+accept gamma INSERTED, direct plain.
#    tdf163894_from_top (24pt paragraph): direct writes REPLACED at 12pt, track at 24pt.
# W4 replace_paragraph: track gives the new text the first replaced run's properties, direct none
# (tdf123054 table cell: track+accept Cell text, direct Cell text).
# W5 replace_paragraph keeps an equation its HTML leaves out, after the new text in track and before it in direct
#    (write:mixed 1000000A). The contract (section 7) refuses the omission unless `delete` lists the equation.
# W6 B8 (README item 10): breaks count as no characters; direct replace_text across a w:br deletes it, track keeps it

# (write:mixed 1000000C select "oneline": track+accept "Line X
two", direct "Line X two").
# W7 revision_settle panics on rich-bare-text.docx (segments.rs:80), as read item 1: see write-engine.tsv.
# W8 read --kind comments lists "ranges":[] for a comment crossing paragraphs (write:mixed comment 1) while the
#    document read lists both ranges; affects both sides' comments projections equally, so no entry here.
# W9 through TOML, an unknown or missing field in ops[1] is reported at ops[0].<field> (parse_plan_toml hard-codes
#    index 0) and other decode errors at "ops".
# W10 an op that needs a malformed part reports it under the wrong name and code: set_list on malformed.docx (its
#    numbering.xml is not well-formed) fails with "document.xml parse failed" (operation_failed); the contract
#    refuses at that op with unreadable_target (section 10).
# W11 delete_paragraphs on a paragraph holding the plan author's own pending insertion nests a w:del inside that
#    w:ins instead of removing it (Word removes your own pending insertion when you delete it); direct mode then
#    accepts the w:del and leaves an empty w:ins pending. write:mixed 10000004 ("Own pending: " + Oracle's w:ins
#    "my insertion" + " then a tail."), direct: docxdriver's read --kind revisions lists {kind ins, text "",
#    locator p4:0-0} and the document read lists 10000005 among the selections; Go removes the insertion, so the
#    revision and the selection entry are gone. Track: docxdriver's w:ins holds a w:del, Go has no w:ins.
# W12 delete_paragraphs wraps only runs, hyperlinks, smart tags and bidi wrappers, so a paragraph-level equation (and
#    a field or custom XML wrapper's runs) stays live and joins the next paragraph. write:mixed, direct, at
#    ["1000000A"] ("Inline math " m:oMath x^2 " between words."): docxdriver's output has 5 m:oMath as the input, the
#    x^2 now first in 1000000B; Go's has 4. No recorded case deletes such a paragraph, so no entry below.
# W13 comment_add anchors at the paragraph's children (anchor_comment_at, paragraph_child_anchor), so a selection inside
#    a hyperlink or a revision wrapper widens to the whole wrapper. write:mixed 10000004 select "insertion" inside the
#    w:ins "my insertion": docxdriver's comments read gives locator p4:13-25 ("my insertion"), Go's p4:16-25
#    ("insertion"), its markers inside the w:ins (CT_RunTrackChange is now tabulated, P4 2026-11-13).
# Not bugs: new paragraph ids derive from the canonical plan, which includes change_mode, so inserted paragraphs get
# different ids in track and direct mode; repaired_ids order in reports changes per run (P4c).
